name: The Unimpressed Critic
why_it_works: A snobby, fictional critic sounds like they are about to tear the product apart, so viewers lean in for the takedown. The misdirection flips: every 'complaint' is secretly the highest praise. That surprise makes the compliment funny instead of braggy, which is the only way a brand can brag and still get a laugh.

hook.pattern: Introduce a famously hard-to-please (fictional) critic who just tried your product, framed like bad news.
examples: The critic tried our {{product}}. It went badly.
The harshest critic in town reviewed our {{product}}.
Bad news. The critic tried the {{product}}.

variables.name: critic_detail
variables.description: One visual detail that makes the fictional critic over-serious
variables.example: a velvet blazer, reading glasses on a chain and a tiny notebook

variables.name: ruined_line
variables.description: The complaint that sounds like a takedown (8 words or fewer, spoken)

variables.name: misdirect_reveal
variables.description: The reveal that the complaint is praise (13 words or fewer, spoken)
variables.example: I can no longer enjoy any other croissant. My life is worse now.

variables.name: tag_action
variables.description: The critic's small hypocritical action that tags the joke, shown in motion (10 words or fewer)
variables.example: quietly slips a second croissant into the blazer pocket

variables.name: critic_tip
variables.description: A real, save-worthy tip for getting the most out of the product (15 words or fewer)
variables.example: Warm it 3 minutes at 350°F. Never the microwave. The critic insists.

variables.name: best_time
variables.description: When to come or order for the best version, from your real schedule (10 words or fewer)
variables.example: Tuesday to Friday, 7 to 8am: first tray, no line.

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer gets for acting (8 words or fewer)

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, copied from the matching pack in compliance/packs.json
variables.example: Results vary. These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA.

craft.technique: Misdirection: a takedown that turns into praise, with a hypocrisy tag
craft.notes: Setup: bad-news framing and a fictional critic played completely straight, so the audience expects a negative review. Turn: the line that sounds like a takedown ('it ruined me') is followed by the reveal that 'ruined' means nothing else compares; the praise arrives disguised as a complaint. Tag: the critic gives zero stars, then sneaks a second one into their pocket; the action contradicts the words, which is the final laugh. Timing: hold the push-in on the glasses coming off for a full second of silence before the ruined line, and in the tag let 'Zero stars.' land, then show the pocket move in one short clip so the action reads without words. Never let the critic smile.

do_not: Base the critic on a real, recognizable reviewer, chef or celebrity
Show fake star ratings or review-site logos that could look like real reviews
Let the critic insult other businesses or customers
Use the misdirection for claims you can't support (skincare: no 'fixed my skin' type results)
compliance: Skincare: the misdirection lines make no skin results, cure or treatment claims; results vary, so no guarantee of any effect; no before/after images
The critic is clearly fictional; never present the review as a real published review or show review-site logos
Restaurants and food: any tip or time shown must match what the business actually serves
